text:
maria: Heads up — customer on Next.js + Turbopack upgraded to @redwood/sdk 2.3.0 and now sees repeated auth failures (401) and exponential client retries in production. Started after a deploy. Repro steps included below.

alex: Ugh. Thanks for flagging. Can you paste the package.json exports map and the build logs? Also Node/Electron/edge runtime?

maria: Node 18.16, Next 14 (turbopack), using server-side rendering and edge functions for some routes. Here's the minimal package.json excerpt they use:```json
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/sdk": "^2.3.0"
  },
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
      "default": "./dist/esm/index.js"
    },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}
```

maria: Build log excerpt:```
[build] WARN  Could not resolve @redwood/sdk (using require fallback)
[build] ERROR Failed to compile server bundle: TypeError: provider.default is not a function
[server] 401 POST /api/infer  - 254ms
[client] 401 from api.redwood.internal: Authorization header missing
```

jamie: The exports map looks odd. Using "default" in exports isn't valid — Node expects conditions like "import" and "require". Bundlers sometimes pick the wrong subpath and strip headers when running in an SSR edge runtime.

sean: Also, Turbopack has known issues where conditional exports fall back to CJS which leads to the SDK being loaded as a plain object instead of an ESM default export. That explains `provider.default is not a function` if code expects `export default`.

alex: Does the customer see the Authorization header present in the outgoing request from their serverless function? The log says header missing — could be our SDK not attaching it because import shape mismatch, or the bundler shim removing Node globals.

maria: I asked them to capture the raw outgoing request in the server runtime. They pasted this snippet from a failing request instrument:```
fetch("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", {
  method: "POST",
  body: "...",
  // headers show undefined in the tracing output, but the code sets token env var
})
```

jamie: Two parallel hypotheses: 1) packaging exports map caused bundler to import CJS variant which doesn't run the auth init path (no header attach) and returns a plain object -> missing method. 2) Turbopack tree-shake or transform removed side-effect code that sets global auth header when bundling for SSR.

alex: Quick repro suggestion for Support -> ask customer to temporarily pin @redwood/sdk@2.2.1, rebuild and redeploy. If errors go away, it's a packaging regression in 2.3.0.

maria: They pinned to 2.2.1 and reported: auth works, no 401s, latency back to normal. So repro seems consistent.

sean: Great. Can you capture `node -p "process.versions"` and `npm ls @redwood/sdk` from their build environment and attach? Also get a minimal repro repo (small Next app) we can run with Turbopack and 2.3.0 to reproduce locally.

maria: Collected: Node v18.16.0, npm 9.8.0. `npm ls @redwood/sdk` shows 2.3.0 at root. I'll ask for a tiny repro repo and add a failing bundle output.

alex: In the meantime, a mitigation: update consumers to use an explicit import form that avoids default import ambiguity, e.g.:```js
import * as Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = Redwood.createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
```
This will work whether the module resolves to CJS or ESM. Document it as a temporary workaround.

jamie: From packaging POV, 2.3.0's package.json likely introduced a nonstandard exports key — using "default" as a condition confuses Node and bundlers. We should roll forward a quick fix: add proper conditional exports:```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```and ensure `type` is consistent and `module`/`main` fields set.

dev-support-bot: Ticket #INC-2026 created and assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P1 (customer-facing auth failures). :rotating_light:

sean: I'll pull a reproducer and try running Turbopack + Next with both versions. If I can reproduce, we'll get a patch out. If not, escalate to packaging team to inspect the published tarball and rollup/tsconfig outputs.

maria: Customer confirmed workaround (pin + import *) is effective for now. They asked for ETA on fix. I'll update ticket and offer to roll back for them if needed.

alex: Action list: 1) eng-runtime to verify published exports/fields in 2.3.0 tarball 2) create minimal repro with Turbopack and 2.3.0 3) patch release with corrected exports map if confirmed 4) notify customers + docs note about import styles and bundler caveats.

jamie: Also add an internal test: run our packaging artifact against a Turbopack/Next emulation to catch this in CI.

maria: Thanks all — will keep channel updated. :eyes:
